classifications.label: Systematic calibration or environmental offset between lab and observatory sites
Environmental or instrumental drift with ~6–8 day periodicity (unresolved in baseline period)
Measurement instrument or readout non-independence—readings reflect a common upstream signal (e.g., shared power supply, cosmic ray burst, or shared environmental sensor) with site-specific coupling
Baseline period is genuinely too short to resolve the timescale structure; data are consistent with i.i.d. noise around per-instrument means, with false peaks from multiple comparisons
Calibration or environmental offset between sites (lab vs. obs) without temporal drift
Unresolved ~6–8 day environmental or instrumental oscillation, invisible in 10-day baseline but manifesting as lagged correlation structure
Weak non-independence between instruments: shared upstream disturbance (power, thermal, cosmic) with site-specific filtering or delay
All observed correlations are statistical artifacts of multiple comparisons; baseline is genuinely too short and noise-like
Residual: unobserved confound (e.g., observer bias in trial selection, instrumental deadtime creating apparent periodicity, or measurement protocol interaction between instruments)
Unresolved ~12–16 day oscillation: invisible in 10-day baseline, manifests as lagged correlation structure
Weak non-independence: shared upstream disturbance (power, thermal, cosmic) differentially filtered by site/instrument
Calibration/environmental offset between lab and obs sites (static, non-drifting) plus independent instrument noise
All observed correlations are statistical artifacts; baseline is too short and data are i.i.d. noise
Unobserved confound: observer bias, instrumental deadtime artifacts, or measurement protocol interaction
Genuine ~12–16 day oscillation: invisible in 10-day baseline, manifests as specific lagged correlations and weak autocorrelations at expected periodic intervals
Weak shared environmental disturbance (power, thermal, cosmic) differentially filtered by site and instrument electronics, producing phase-shifted weak correlations
Static calibration offset between lab and obs sites plus instrument-specific noise; lagged correlations are statistical artifacts arising from limited baseline and multiple offset testing
All observed correlations, including lag-3 peak, are statistical artifacts: false discovery from testing ~30 offset combinations per pair and multiple instrument pairs
Unobserved confound in measurement protocol: systematic batching, recording delay, or observer selection bias creating false lagged structure without physical signal
